rv.q: What a compelling project and what vibrant life here is given to a mostly lost Chicago play!
The performances are some of the best acting I've seen all year.
Court Theatre has given Chicago audiences a gift in reviving Theodore Ward's masterpiece.
All of them bring a unique and phenomenal energy to the production, which was intriguing throughout the two hours and 10 minutes.

Court Theatre's stirring revival of Ward's landmark 1938 drama, Big White Fog , directed by Ron OJ Parson, makes the case for why that's a shame, and why Ward's work deserves fresh eyes and audiences in the 21st century.
The seventeen-player ensemble is exactly that—an actor's ensemble to the end. They feed off each other well, and each leaves a strong, individual mark.
Overall, 'Big White Fog' is an engaging and thought-provoking production that tackles themes of hope, sacrifice, and the enduring struggle for a better life.
